docs.title: Overview
docs.text: What Open AD Kit is, why it exists, and how it relates to the Autoware ecosystem: the software it packages for cloud-native deployment.

docs.title: What is Open AD Kit
docs.text:
Open AD Kit packages the Autoware autonomous driving stack as focused, independently deployable container images. Instead of one monolithic image, it splits the stack along the AD pipeline — sensing, perception, localization, mapping, planning, control, vehicle system, API, simulation, visualization, and the CARLA bridge — so you run only what a workload needs.

Autoware provides the autonomy stack; Open AD Kit makes it deployable. It packages upstream software into composable images, defines deployment configurations, integrates target platforms, and maintains the build, test, and release tooling that keeps deployments consistent from one host to the next. It ships simulation deployments today; a supported path to a real vehicle interface is on the roadmap.

It also integrates Autoware Safety Island, which runs on real-time operating systems and automotive hardware rather than in a container. Open AD Kit is the first SOAFEE blueprint for the software-defined vehicle; Supported Platforms covers the derived blueprints and the platform tiers.

docs.title: Why Open AD Kit
docs.text:
Modular Components

Independent images for each stage of the AD pipeline. Deploy only what you need.

Mixed Criticality

Keep safety-critical control on the Safety Island's real-time hardware, beside the containerized stack.

Cloud Native

Scale from simulation to the edge with containerized deployments, reproducible image builds, and platform integrations.

Connected and Continuous

CI/CD with GitHub Actions, optimized build caching, and containerized testing.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
Open AD Kit runs Autoware as a pipeline of containerized components. Each container handles one stage of autonomous driving, and the stages communicate over ROS 2 DDS on the host network.

  1. Sensing captures and preprocesses raw sensor data (LiDAR, camera, IMU).
  2. Perception detects and tracks objects, traffic lights, and drivable space.
  3. Mapping serves high-definition map data that the rest of the stack consumes.
  4. Localization determines the vehicle's exact position on the map.
  5. Planning computes a safe, feasible trajectory to the goal.
  6. Control converts that trajectory into throttle, brake, and steering commands.
  7. Vehicle System bridges those commands to the actual vehicle or simulator.

A deployment runs the subset of these stages a task needs. Autoware Safety Island joins the same pipeline over DDS, adding a safety-critical actuation path alongside the containerized services.

docs.title: Key Terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Component image A published container image holding one or more Autoware functions, for example planning. Deployment A named, ready-to-run stack: a manifest, environment files, and Compose configuration for a task such as planning simulation. Deployment manifest The deployment.json file that tells the CLI how to run a deployment: requirements, data downloads, and one-shot services. Kit manifest The openadkit.json file of a kit: what it extends, its deployments and the images it pins. Kit An openadkit.json and its deployments: the reference kit or an integrator's differences over a pinned base release. extends / base The kit's pinned Open AD Kit release and the reference deployment it includes. Config override Parameter/file differences layered over package configuration; not a copy of the full base file. Overlay workspace Custom ROS packages built against the matching pinned devel image and sourced over the base. Node A deployment's host-local view, with its own services, Compose project, ROS domain and Zenoh endpoint. Evidence The evidence cells run against one build; the release gate requires a successful run that passed every cell. Evidence cell One runtime test of a deployment on one ROS distro and topology, such as planning-simulation-humble-linux-amd64. CI exemption A reasoned manifest entry for a deployment without hosted runtime evidence, not a passing-test claim. BOM The release's pinned Autoware input, component images and external images. Latest alias An image tag such as planning-humble that follows the newest stable release. Release tags (-vX.Y.Z) and digests stay immutable. Digest pin An image reference by content hash (@sha256:…) instead of a tag, so the same image bits are always used. Mixed criticality Running safety-critical and non-critical workloads on separately qualified execution environments. Here, the Safety Island's real-time hardware beside the containerized stack; the containers on one host share its network and are not isolated by criticality.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
Last reviewed: 2026-11-09, before v2.0.0.

What Open AD Kit plans next. Finished work leaves this page and appears in the release notes.

docs.title: Now: v2.0.0
docs.text:
1. Consistent readiness. One readiness and failure policy for run and restart, covering healthchecks, crashes and one-shot services.
  2. Development loop in CI. The example kit's check edits a ROS package, builds it, restarts the affected services and verifies the change.
  3. Image contents. Each image carries only the build inputs and runtime packages it needs, before v2.0.0 makes its contents part of the contract.
  4. Stable interface. Document what SemVer covers, from commands, exit codes and manifests to image tags and data paths, and mark experimental features.
  5. Release. A full build and evidence run, then a clean-host install, kit, restart and upgrade check on a release candidate.

docs.title: Next: v2.x, in priority order
docs.text:
1. One resolved configuration. Resolve settings and the Compose model once; data paths, images, mounts and validation use the same result.
  2. Development tooling. A devcontainer and a debugging guide for the development loop.
  3. Comparable regression results. A fixed scenario set whose latency, resource use and driving metrics are compared with a baseline.
  4. Platform evidence. Native arm64 evidence cells and GPU logging simulation coverage.
  5. Autoware upgrades. Measure clean common-image builds on a 4-vCPU runner before the next Autoware version change.
  6. Image SBOMs. A software bill of materials for each container image.
  7. Autoware main canary. A weekly, non-blocking build against Autoware main, kept out of releases and PR checks.
  8. Upstream build fixes. Propose upstream the dependency fixes that the image boundaries need.
  9. CES 2027 demo. Hardware integration and partner evidence for the demonstrated setup; tracked in #169.

docs.title: Later: direction, not commitment
docs.text:
• Autoware System Designer. It selects launch files and parameters; Open AD Kit selects images and Compose services. See Autoware System Designer.
  • Path to a vehicle. A vehicle-interface contract and reference hardware, a validation ladder from SIL to full-scale vehicles, and offline OCI delivery.
  • Visualizer. KasmVNC in place of TigerVNC, noVNC and Openbox; Lichtblick with foxglove_bridge for analysis and bag playback.
  • rmw_zenoh. Replace zenoh-bridge-ros2dds for split-host on Jazzy if an evaluation succeeds.
  • Safety Island on CARLA. A kit with the Safety Island's closed loop over CAN, backed by its own runtime evidence.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text: No custom OTA service, Kubernetes stack, fork of upstream workloads, or ASIL or NCAP certification claim. Safety Island owns its safety boundary; Open AD Kit integrates it.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
Open AD Kit packages Autoware Universe into focused container images. Each image groups closely related Autoware functions, and deployments run them as separate containers that talk over ROS 2. External clients use the Autoware AD API; the images use Autoware's component interfaces between them.

All images build on a shared universe-common layer; see Build from Source for the build graph. The image reference lists tags and platforms.

docs.title: Sensing & Perception
docs.text:
Sensor preprocessing and environment understanding in one image.

  • Sensing — LiDAR distortion correction, filtering, and point cloud preprocessing; camera and radar preprocessing; GNSS/INS preprocessing; shared point cloud container. Launch: component_sensing.launch.xml
  • Perception — camera, LiDAR, and radar object detection and fusion; multi-object tracking and trajectory prediction; traffic light recognition; occupancy grid mapping. Launch: component_perception.launch.xml
  • CUDA variant — sensing-perception-cuda accelerates point cloud processing and neural-network inference on NVIDIA GPUs. It is amd64-only and requires the NVIDIA Container Toolkit. Used by Logging Simulation (--gpu) and CARLA Simulation.

docs.title: Localization & Mapping
docs.text:
Serves HD maps and estimates the vehicle pose within them.

  • Localization — GNSS/RTK positioning and IMU dead reckoning; visual odometry and LiDAR map matching; automatic pose initialization; EKF state estimation. Launch: component_localization.launch.xml
  • Mapping — Lanelet2 vector map and point cloud map serving; occupancy grid and point cloud map construction; map coordinate transforms. Launch: component_map.launch.xml

Planning and Scenario Simulation run only the map service; the simulator supplies map-to-odometry transforms. Logging and CARLA Simulation also run localization.

docs.title: Planning
docs.text:
Trajectory generation: route planning on Lanelet2 road networks; behavior planning for lanes, intersections, and obstacles; kinematically feasible motion planning; goal and parking maneuvers; the planning validator that publishes /planning/trajectory. Launch: component_planning.launch.xml

  • CUDA variant — planning-cuda builds the same packages with CUDA and TensorRT, so planning_setting:=diffusion_planner runs Autoware 2.0's Diffusion Planner. It is amd64-only and requires the NVIDIA Container Toolkit. Used by Planning Simulation (--gpu).

docs.title: Control
docs.text: Vehicle control from /planning/trajectory: lateral steering and longitudinal velocity control; PID and Model Predictive Control modes; vehicle-specific command conversion; emergency stop and heartbeat monitoring. Control reads only that trajectory, so it stays the same whichever planner produces it. Launch: component_control.launch.xml

docs.title: Vehicle and System
docs.text:
Vehicle actuation and system diagnostics, run as separate containers from one image.

  • Vehicle — actuation and state reporting; steering, throttle, brake, gear, and turn-signal conversion; vehicle dimensions, limits, and kinematic parameters. Launch: tier4_vehicle_launch/vehicle.launch.xml
  • System — health monitoring and heartbeat management; diagnostic aggregation; Minimum Risk Maneuver handling; CPU, memory, and process monitoring. Launch: tier4_system_component.launch.xml

docs.title: API
docs.text:
Packages the Autoware AD API used by fleet managers, HMIs, and scenario runners. It provides ROS 2 services and topics for:

  • vehicle position, velocity, engage status, and operation mode
  • autonomous, manual, stop, local, and remote mode transitions
  • route and goal setting
  • emergency stop and engage/disengage commands
  • scenario simulation auto-engage and route integration

Launch: tier4_autoware_api_component.launch.xml. It is the standard external entry point for the modular simulation deployments.

docs.title: Simulator
docs.text:
Closed-loop vehicle and environment simulation without real sensors or vehicle hardware:

  • configurable kinematic and dynamic vehicle models
  • dummy perception, vehicle, door, and traffic-infrastructure interfaces
  • Scenario Simulator v2 adapter and localization simulation mode
  • simulated point cloud preprocessing, object tracking, shape estimation, and map-based prediction
  • occupancy and elevation map handling; vehicle command conversion

Launch: tier4_simulator_component.launch.xml, with the perception simulation (dummy objects, tracking, prediction and the occupancy grid map) in its own perception-simulation service from planning_simulator/perception_simulation.launch.xml. On amd64 it also carries the CARLA bridge and the CARLA Python client that the CARLA Simulation deployment runs in its carla-interface service.

docs.title: Visualizer
docs.text:
Browser-accessible RViz2 through noVNC: RViz2 with Autoware plugins, Openbox, TigerVNC, and a noVNC server over plain HTTP. The VNC backend stays loopback-only, and so does noVNC by default; reach it remotely through an SSH tunnel. To serve HTTPS, mount your own certificate into the visualizer from an integrator kit or a Compose override (the release mounts none) and name its files in NOVNC_CERT and NOVNC_KEY; it stays the same across starts, so a browser exception for it holds.

Variable Default Values Description RVIZ_CONFIG /tmp/openadkit/autoware_launch/share/autoware_launch/rviz/autoware.rviz Path RViz2 configuration inside the container; the default is the copy with config overrides applied REMOTE_DISPLAY true true, false Use browser-based RViz2; false opens RViz2 on the desktop, using the session's DISPLAY and XAUTHORITY REMOTE_PASSWORD — String Required when REMOTE_DISPLAY=true WEBSOCKIFY_BIND 127.0.0.1 IP address noVNC bind address; bridge networking uses 0.0.0.0 with a host loopback port mapping USE_SIM_TIME false true, false Use the ROS simulation clock RVIZ_GPU auto auto, on, off Automatic, forced, or disabled VirtualGL acceleration NOVNC_CERT, NOVNC_KEY unset Paths Certificate and key inside the container; set both to serve HTTPS only

For access and remote use, see the Quickstart.

docs.title: CARLA Interface
docs.text:
The simulator image's autoware_carla_interface translates Autoware control commands to CARLA and CARLA sensor data to ROS 2 messages:

  • CARLA world initialization and synchronous simulation
  • ego vehicle spawning and sensor-kit configuration
  • camera, LiDAR, IMU, and GNSS message translation
  • vehicle command calibration and traffic light state publication
  • lightweight sensor mappings for constrained hosts

Launch: autoware_carla_interface.launch.xml. CARLA publishes its Python client for x86_64 only, so only the amd64 simulator image has it (Humble and Jazzy); the CARLA Simulation deployment is Humble-only and needs an NVIDIA GPU.

docs.title: Deployments
docs.text:
A deployment is a ready-to-run Autoware stack for one task. New users should start with Planning Simulation.

Deployment Purpose GPU Planning Simulation Plan and follow a route on a demo map Optional Scenario Simulation Run predefined traffic scenarios No Logging Simulation Replay recorded sensor data through sensing, perception, and localization Recommended CARLA Simulation Drive a CARLA vehicle in closed loop Required Split-host simulation Run Autoware on one host and the simulator on another over Zenoh CARLA only Safety Island Simulation Planning Simulation driven by the Autoware Safety Island controller instead of Autoware's trajectory follower No

docs.title: Running a Deployment
docs.text:
Complete the Quickstart setup first.

Commands on this page are shown as installed by the release installer. From a source checkout, prefix them with ./ and run them from the repository root.

openadkit list
openadkit run planning-simulation
openadkit status
openadkit logs --follow
openadkit stop
  • Add --ros-distro jazzy to validate, fetch, or run to select Jazzy; Humble is the default.
  • Add --gpu for the optional GPU mode of Planning Simulation (the Diffusion Planner) or Logging Simulation (CenterPoint). CARLA needs a GPU, so its GPU mode turns on by itself; it is Humble-only.
  • Add --node to validate or run to start one node of a split-host run. status, logs, and stop find the running node themselves; they take --node only when several nodes of one deployment run on the same machine.
  • Put host settings in ~/.config/openadkit/<name>.env; see Configuration.

Scenario split-node evidence covers two isolated nodes on one hosted runner. CARLA is explicitly exempt from hosted runtime CI. Neither is a claim of arbitrary two-machine or vehicle compatibility; see the evidence policy.

To build your own stack, start a kit with openadkit new (Create a Kit). It keeps its own kit manifest and deployment in one directory, extending a deployment without copying it.

docs.title: Create a Kit
docs.text:
Start your own kit with openadkit new. It makes a kit that extends this Open AD Kit and one of its deployments without copying them, so the kit keeps only your differences:

openadkit new my-kit                       # on top of planning-simulation
openadkit new my-kit --base scenario-simulation

docs.title: One Directory, One Deployment
docs.text:
my-kit/
├── openadkit.json
├── deployment.json
├── docker-compose.yaml
├── config.env
├── config/autoware/
└── overlay_ws/src/
  • openadkit.json selects the base (extends), lists extra images you pin (externalImages), and points the my-kit deployment at ".", this same directory.
  • deployment.json names the base deployment and the Compose entrypoint. Architecture, ROS distro, GPU, downloads and the verify step are inherited.
  • docker-compose.yaml includes ${OPENADKIT_BASE_DEPLOYMENT}/docker-compose.yaml; add your services below it. OPENADKIT_BASE_ROOT names the base root for shared assets.
  • config.env holds only the values you change, such as VEHICLE_ID.
  • config/autoware/ holds parameter overrides for Autoware packages.
  • overlay_ws/src/ holds your ROS packages.

The directory name, the deployment key in openadkit.json and name in deployment.json agree; rename them together. The CLI checks that they agree.

docs.title: Pin Your Base
docs.text: openadkit new from an installed release writes its version, such as "extends": "v2.0.0"; the kit then runs with that release's own launcher. From a source checkout it writes the checkout's path. To move to another release, change extends; the next command in the kit downloads that release if it is missing.

docs.title: Build, Validate, Run, Stop
docs.text:
cd my-kit
openadkit build                 # overlay_ws, in the release's devel image
openadkit validate my-kit
openadkit run my-kit --verify   # start, wait until ready, run the base's end-to-end check
openadkit stop

A source checkout pins no devel image: set DEVEL_IMAGE to the matching universe-common-devel digest from that build's metadata before build. Add --ros-distro jazzy to build, validate and run for Jazzy. Static validation renders the Compose model; it is not runtime or ABI evidence. CI makes a kit with openadkit new and exercises every extension point on Humble and Jazzy: a value, a parameter override, a C++ package, a pinned image and a service with a healthcheck, then Planning Simulation's drive-to-goal check.

Keep parameter and package changes in config/ and overlay_ws/ rather than mounting over /opt/autoware or replacing base service commands. See the Integrator Guide for configuration order, pinned image replacement and contract warnings.

docs.title: Integrator Guide
docs.text: An integrator kit owns its differences, while Open AD Kit owns the base CLI, images and deployments. Start one with openadkit new (Create a Kit); the kit CI exercises is that output with the example fixture on top. This interface requires manifest schema version 2; older manifests are rejected.

docs.title: Pin the Base
docs.text:
Set kind to kit and extends to a published schema-v2 release tag in your root openadkit.json. The CLI locates that version under ~/.local/share/openadkit/openadkit-<tag> and delegates to its launcher. A missing version is downloaded and verified on first use, like a build tool's wrapper does; your active openadkit stays as it is. OPENADKIT_INSTALL_DIR overrides the install root for both.

A relative or absolute source path is also accepted for development. Only one level of extends is supported: a kit extends Open AD Kit, not another kit. Each kit deployment names a base deployment in the pinned release. Its architecture, ROS distro and GPU requirements are inherited without narrowing or widening. Base downloads and one-shot reset services are inherited; a kit can add downloads with distinct destination variables and extra reset services. Kit deployments currently use the single-host Compose view, not inherited split-host nodes.

A kit made by openadkit new my-kit has just one deployment, also named my-kit. Its openadkit.json, deployment.json, Compose and differences live in one directory; deployments.my-kit.path is ".". No nested deployments/ directory is needed. Run commands from that directory, not the base repository.

docs.title: 1. Values
docs.text:
Put only differences in your deployment's config.env. Compose interpolation reads these files in order (later wins):

  1. Base config.env
  2. Base config.gpu.env, when GPU mode is selected
  3. Kit config.env, if present
  4. Kit config.gpu.env, if present and GPU mode is selected
  5. ~/.config/openadkit/<kit-deployment>.env, if present

Container ROS/DDS defaults come from the included services' runtime.env. Shell exports do not hide values in the configuration files. The CLI injects the ROS distro, host UID/GID, overlay mount paths, OPENADKIT_BASE_ROOT (the base root) and OPENADKIT_BASE_DEPLOYMENT (the directory selected by base); release component images and external images remain pinned.

docs.title: 2. Config Overrides
docs.text:
Store overrides under config/autoware/<package>/<path-relative-to-package-share>. For example, config/autoware/autoware_control_config/config/lane_departure_checker/lane_departure_checker.param.yaml:

/**:
  ros__parameters:
    update_rate: 20.0

On each start, the entrypoint hook copies the package share directory into /tmp/openadkit/<package>/share/<package>. It applies the shared, base-deployment and kit-deployment layers in that order. YAML mappings merge recursively; scalars and lists replace the old value. Launch substitutions such as $(var ...) stay intact. Non-YAML files replace their counterpart.

The copied prefixes go first on AMENT_PREFIX_PATH, and base launch arguments use the same stable paths. No change is written into the image. Removing an override and restarting returns to the remaining layers.

Unknown packages, files or YAML keys are warnings, not startup failures. The hook logs them and writes /tmp/openadkit/overlay-report.json in each container. Once the services are up, run collects those reports and warns about every override without a counterpart: a package no service has changes nothing, and a file or a parameter its package does not have is added. That is intended for a new file such as a diagnostics graph; after a base version change it usually means a renamed package, file or parameter. Every service gets the same layers, so a package installed in only some images is not reported.

docs.title: A New Vehicle
docs.text:
Autoware's defaults describe a passenger car. Review these for your vehicle; their package and path depend on the base's Autoware version, so look them up in its images and check run's override warnings.

Parameters File Why Dimensions, wheel_base, max_steer_angle vehicle_info.param.yaml of your vehicle description Planning and control use them as limits; a steering limit above the vehicle's makes control ask for angles it cannot reach. Sensor poses your sensor kit's sensor_kit_calibration.yaml and sensors_calibration.yaml A wrong sign or offset shows up as a localization error of the same size. nominal_latency, assumed_limit_acc control_validator.param.yaml Your actuation latency and achievable braking. With car values a slower or weaker vehicle fails validation and triggers an MRM. pose_measurement.pose_gate_dist ekf_localizer.param.yaml The Mahalanobis gate for pose updates. A start pose far from the truth can be rejected for good. Velocity, acceleration, jerk and steering-rate limits vehicle_cmd_gate.param.yaml The last limits before the vehicle interface.

docs.title: 3. Overlay Workspace
docs.text:
Put ROS packages in overlay_ws/src and build them in the universe-common-devel image from the same build as your runtime images. A release pins that image next to its runtime images, so the CLI builds with the right one:

openadkit build [--ros-distro humble]   # in the kit: its overlay_ws
openadkit build PATH                    # any workspace, with the pins of the kit around it
openadkit build -- --packages-select my_pkg                # arguments after -- go to colcon build
openadkit build -- --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug   # Release unless you set another

Packages build incrementally: a second build compiles only what changed. The hook sources the workspace on top of Autoware, so a package with the name of an Autoware package comes first; Autoware packages that link against its library keep the copy they were built with. --install-base and --build-base stay fixed: the services source install/ where they mount the workspace.

The CLI records the image and distro in install/.openadkit-overlay.json, and validate and run warn after a base upgrade or a distro change until you rebuild. Such a rebuild starts from a clean build/ and install/, since CMake caches record the paths they were configured with. A source checkout pins no devel image: set DEVEL_IMAGE to the matching universe-common-devel digest from the build metadata. The hook sources overlay_ws/install/local_setup.bash on top of Autoware.

The workspace belongs to the kit: the one overlay_ws at the kit root serves every deployment of the kit, since they all extend one base and its images. Every Autoware service mounts it, and the hook sources it on top of Autoware, so its packages are visible in every service. Whether your code runs depends on what starts it:

  • A changed copy of an Autoware package shadows the image's own. It runs where Autoware already launches that package, with nothing more to configure.
  • A new node runs only where something starts it: an extra service (as the example fixture's acme-probe), a launch file you override under config/autoware, or by hand with openadkit shell <service> ros2 run <package> <node>.

To try a workspace with a reference deployment, without writing a kit, mount it with --ws:

openadkit build ~/my_ws
openadkit run planning-simulation --ws ~/my_ws

--ws is for a deployment without a workspace of its own; on a kit that has one it is an error rather than a second layer.

The devel and runtime images install ROS packages from the same ROS snapshot, so an overlay built in the devel image links the ROS versions the runtime image ships. A dependency you add must also exist in the runtime image; the overlay cannot install packages. The example fixture's C++ node links diagnostic_updater deliberately to test the devel/runtime ABI boundary, then publishes /acme/probe.

docs.title: 4. Extra Services
docs.text:
Include the base's Compose file using OPENADKIT_BASE_DEPLOYMENT, then define your services under services:. Keep communicating ROS services on the base ROS domain and middleware. An extra Open AD Kit runtime service loads the kit workspace by mounting ${OPENADKIT_OVERLAY_WS} at /openadkit/overlay_ws:ro, as the example fixture's acme-probe does. It needs no image of its own: a runtime image and the workspace are enough. Build your own image only for what the runtime images lack, such as a system package or a non-ROS application, and declare it as an external image (point 5).

To replace one side of a base that runs as split-host nodes, include only the other side's service layer instead of the base's Compose file. For example, a kit that brings its own simulator to carla-simulation includes ${OPENADKIT_BASE_DEPLOYMENT}/services.autoware.yaml: no service in it depends on a CARLA service. The base's resetServices that the kit's services leave out are skipped; the kit's own must exist.

docs.title: 5. Image Replacement
docs.text:
Declare the images your kit uses but does not build in its externalImages, each with either one digest-pinned ref or a distros map of digest-pinned references. A name matching a component image variable replaces that component; other names supply images for new services. Use ${NAME:?} in Compose to require the declared reference.

A replaced base image needs your own runtime evidence: pinning alone does not prove that it honors the entrypoint, launch or parameter interfaces.

docs.title: Validation and Evidence
docs.text:
openadkit validate <deployment> renders the deployment and checks its manifest and data. It does not pull images or prove that the runtime works; run reports overrides without a counterpart (see Config Overrides).

Your kit's acceptance checks run where CI runs them:

  • Readiness: give a service of your own a Compose healthcheck. run waits until it passes. The example fixture's acme-probe service runs checks/example_kit.py, which checks the fresh /acme/probe publication of its C++ package and its parameters.
  • End to end: the base's verify step runs on top of your layer with openadkit run --verify. To check something else, name your own in deployment.json: {"verify": {"service": "<service>", "command": [...]}} runs the command in that running service, and without command the step waits for the service to exit and takes its exit code.

The example kit's evidence cell runs both: its healthcheck and Planning Simulation's drive-to-goal check. Humble and Jazzy each build the workspace against their matching devel digest.

A base deployment's CI exemption stays with the kit; an exemption is not runtime evidence. The release gate requires PASSED. See Evidence Workflow for reusing the verifier; it does not yet accept arbitrary external kits.

docs.title: Upgrade Without Losing Your Work
docs.text: Install the new base next to the old version, update extends, rebuild your workspace against its devel digest, then validate and run your acceptance checks. Your repository, host config, downloaded data and output directories are outside the base release. Updating the default launcher does not change a kit's explicit version pin. See CLI & Maintenance for the config and output directories and marker-protected data cleanup.

docs.title: Split-host simulation (Zenoh)
docs.text:
Run the Autoware stack on one lab machine and the simulator on another. Each workload keeps its catalog name and declares its nodes in deployment.json; each machine starts one node with --node.

  • scenario-simulation: --node autoware on one host, --node scenario on the other.
  • carla-simulation: --node autoware on one GPU host, --node carla on the other.

Omitting --node keeps today's single-host graph.

The manifest selects compose.<node>.yaml. Each entrypoint explicitly includes its workload services and ../shared/compose.zenoh.yaml, and mounts its own config/zenoh.json5 allowlist. The CLI adds no services or Zenoh-specific paths. The allowlist is an explicit node requiredFiles entry: missing or symlinked files fail validation before starting containers, without Zenoh-specific CLI logic. It selects the declared files, image references and env files, and supplies the node's rosDomainId as OPENADKIT_ROS_DOMAIN_ID.

Each node is isolated: its own Compose project (openadkit-<deployment>_<node>), its own container names, and its own ROS domain (rosDomainId in the manifest). The nodes only see each other through the Zenoh bridge, so both nodes can also run on one machine for testing, as long as each listens on its own port (see below).

DDS stays local (CYCLONEDDS_NETWORK_INTERFACE=lo, applied by both the workload containers and the bridge; a node ignores another interface in the host settings file). Only ROS traffic selected by the workload allowlist crosses Zenoh: simulation time, vehicle status and commands, transforms, ADAPI calls, and the enabled sensors. Map blobs, camera images, and the visualization/teleop traffic are not routed.

Evidence scope

Split-host nodes ship in the release. Scenario Simulation's required split cell tests two isolated nodes on one hosted runner; CARLA is explicitly exempt from hosted runtime CI. Existing observations include:

  • Both node views are rendered and validated in CI (docker compose config).
  • On one host, the two scenario-simulation nodes pass the sample scenario over Zenoh, and the scenario node's ROS domain sees no Autoware nodes, only the bridged topics.
  • On a lab pair, sample scenarios pass and a CARLA goal reaches ArrivedGoal over the bridge.

Bridge restart resilience and recorded CARLA throughput and latency evidence are still open. One-runner evidence is not a general two-host, WAN or vehicle compatibility claim; see the release policy.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
On both hosts:

  • Host setup via Getting Started.
  • The same Open AD Kit release and ROS distro on both machines.
  • Layer-2/3 connectivity between the hosts and 7447/tcp open only between them. Topic allowlists are not authentication; do not expose the port to a WAN.

Fetch data on the hosts that mount it:

openadkit fetch scenario-simulation   # both hosts (the runner bind-mounts MAP_PATH)
openadkit fetch carla-simulation      # Autoware host only (the map is autoware-scoped)

docs.title: Configure the bridge endpoints
docs.text:
Create or edit ~/.config/openadkit/<workload>.env on each host. Use the host's LAN IP, not 0.0.0.0:

Host Variables Autoware (--node autoware) ZENOH_LISTEN=tcp/<autoware-host-ip>:7447 Simulator (--node scenario or --node carla) ZENOH_LISTEN=tcp/<sim-host-ip>:7447 and ZENOH_PEER=tcp/<autoware-host-ip>:7447

The Autoware node is listen-only and starts first. validate and run on the connecting node fail fast when ZENOH_PEER is unset; stop, status, and logs never need either variable.

To run both nodes on one machine, pass the endpoints per command instead, with a separate port for each node:

ZENOH_LISTEN=tcp/127.0.0.1:7447 openadkit run scenario-simulation --node autoware
ZENOH_LISTEN=tcp/127.0.0.1:7448 ZENOH_PEER=tcp/127.0.0.1:7447 \
  openadkit run scenario-simulation --node scenario

docs.title: Scenario simulation
docs.text:
Start Autoware first:

# Autoware host
openadkit run scenario-simulation --node autoware

Then the scenario host:

openadkit run scenario-simulation --node scenario

The runner waits up to SCENARIO_READY_TIMEOUT for Autoware readiness over Zenoh before launching the scenario. Results are written on the scenario host under ~/openadkit-output/scenario-simulation/results. The visualizer runs on the scenario host too, so RViz takes no CPU or GPU from Autoware on the edge; noVNC is loopback-only (WEBSOCKIFY_BIND), so remote desks use an SSH tunnel.

Stop each host; the CLI finds the live node from its Compose project:

openadkit stop

docs.title: CARLA
docs.text:
Both hosts need an NVIDIA GPU. Start Autoware first:

# Autoware host
openadkit run carla-simulation --node autoware

Then the CARLA host:

openadkit run carla-simulation --node carla

CARLA RPC (127.0.0.1:2000) and map loading stay local to the CARLA host. The interface publishes simulation time, the enabled lidar/IMU/GNSS sensors, vehicle status, and transforms; Autoware publishes control commands. Cameras are disabled in sensor_mapping.yaml; enabling them requires an allowlist and throughput update. The visualizer runs on the CARLA host, where the raw LiDAR already originates.

docs.title: Allowlist
docs.text:
Each workload ships its Zenoh allowlist in deployments/<workload>/config/zenoh.json5, mounted into the bridge of every node. Entries are full-name regular expressions, not globs. Both hosts use the same file: either side can own an endpoint. Review the list before routing anything new, and keep the host boundary on the lab LAN: the allowlist is not authentication.

Both allowlists also carry what the visualizer on the simulator host shows: planning and control output, objects, the vector map marker, /robot_description and the ADAPI (/api/.*) its panels use. Zenoh sends a topic across only when the other host subscribes to it, so without a visualizer these stay on the edge. The processed CARLA pointclouds cross at 2 Hz (pub_max_frequencies), and the pointcloud map is not bridged. A visualizer on the edge is the single-host mode.

The split scenario cell checks that every allowlisted topic exists in one of the two graphs, so an Autoware rename fails CI instead of silently stopping a topic. CI cannot run CARLA: check its allowlist against the live graph of a two-host run after an Autoware update.

The scenario allowlist carries the simple sensor simulator's /sensing/imu/imu_data because autonomous emergency braking and autonomous-mode availability on the Autoware host depend on it; without it the vehicle stays in PLANNING and the scenario times out.

docs.title: Latency and timing
docs.text: Cross-host simulation is timing sensitive. With a large round-trip time the TF stream jitters and control nodes log transform or collision-detector warnings even when scenarios still pass. Keep both hosts on the same lab LAN; WAN and VPN links are best-effort and are not the supported setup.

docs.title: Lifecycle notes
docs.text:
• stop, status, and logs find the live node from its Compose project, so you normally omit --node. When several nodes of one deployment run on the same machine, status and stop act on all of them; pass --node to choose one for the other commands.
  • Re-running a live node updates it in place. Starting the single-host graph while a node is live, or a node while the single-host graph is live, is refused: stop it first.
  • Do not restart a single bridge or interface container while the split is live: route churn can leave a bridged topic half-connected until both hosts restart. Stop and start the node instead (see Troubleshooting).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
If RViz shows no Auto button and /api/operation_mode/change_to_autonomous answers "The target mode is not available", a bridged vehicle-status topic has stopped flowing:

  • Diagnosis on the Autoware host: a state monitor logs a bridge topic timeout (for example /vehicle/status/steering_status topic is timeout), and /system/command_mode/availability reports autonomous mode unavailable.
  • Cause: restarting a single bridge or interface container in a live split can leave Zenoh routes half-created (a route is removed and not recreated), so the topic no longer crosses.
  • Remedy: stop the workload on both hosts and start the nodes again (openadkit stop, then openadkit run <name> --node ...). A clean restart restores the routes.

docs.title: CARLA Simulation
docs.text: Run the full modular Autoware stack against CARLA 0.9.16 in closed loop.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• amd64 host with Ubuntu 22.04 (CARLA 0.9.16 is not validated on 24.04)
  • NVIDIA GPU with the Vulkan ICD at /usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/nvidia_icd.json
  • ROS 2 Humble images; this deployment does not support Jazzy

Install Docker and the NVIDIA toolkit once, as described in the Quickstart, with GPU support:

openadkit setup --gpu --verify

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
Commands on this page are shown as installed by the release installer. From a source checkout, prefix them with ./ and run them from the repository root.

openadkit run carla-simulation

run downloads and verifies the Town01 map, then starts CARLA and the Autoware stack. CARLA renders offscreen by default.

To run Autoware and CARLA on separate hosts, see Split-host simulation.

config/sensor_mapping.yaml enables LiDAR, IMU, and GNSS. Camera entries are available but commented out.

docs.title: Open the Visualizer
docs.text:
Open http://localhost:6080/vnc.html and sign in with the default password openadkit. Set your own REMOTE_PASSWORD in ~/.config/openadkit/<deployment>.env.

For a remote host, forward the port over SSH and open http://localhost:8080/vnc.html locally:

ssh -L 8080:localhost:6080 <user>@<host>

In RViz2, set a goal with 2D Goal Pose and select Auto.

docs.title: Stop and Recover
docs.text:
openadkit stop

Run stop also after a failed start, to release the GPU. If autonomous mode is unavailable, inspect /system/command_mode/availability and /diagnostics_graph/status. For other issues, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Logging Simulation
docs.text:
Replay a demo rosbag through sensing, perception, and localization. An NVIDIA GPU with at least 4 GB VRAM is recommended; CPU mode works but is much slower.

Complete the Quickstart setup first. For GPU mode, run openadkit setup --gpu --verify.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
Commands on this page are shown as installed by the release installer. From a source checkout, prefix them with ./ and run them from the repository root.

openadkit run logging-simulation         # CPU: clustering-based detection
openadkit run logging-simulation --gpu   # GPU: CenterPoint on CUDA (amd64 only)

Add --ros-distro jazzy to select Jazzy; Humble is the default.

run downloads the sample map and rosbag, and with --gpu also the CenterPoint models (to ~/autoware_data/lidar_centerpoint). The rosbag starts playing once Autoware is ready.

The demo rosbag is Copyright 2020 TIER IV, Inc. It has no camera images, so traffic-light recognition is unavailable and detection is less complete than with a full recording.

docs.title: Open the Visualizer
docs.text:
Open http://localhost:6080/vnc.html and sign in with the default password openadkit. Set your own REMOTE_PASSWORD in ~/.config/openadkit/<deployment>.env.

For a remote host, forward the port over SSH and open http://localhost:8080/vnc.html locally:

ssh -L 8080:localhost:6080 <user>@<host>

openadkit stop

To replace missing sample data, run openadkit fetch logging-simulation --force; it also refreshes the CenterPoint models. For other issues, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Planning Simulation
docs.text:
Run the Autoware planning and control stack on a demo map with the built-in simulator, then set a route in browser-based RViz2. No GPU is required; with an NVIDIA GPU, --gpu plans with Autoware 2.0's Diffusion Planner.

Complete the Quickstart setup first. For GPU mode, run openadkit setup --gpu --verify.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
Commands on this page are shown as installed by the release installer. From a source checkout, prefix them with ./ and run them from the repository root.

openadkit run planning-simulation         # CPU: the rule-based planner
openadkit run planning-simulation --gpu   # GPU: the Diffusion Planner (amd64 only)

Add --ros-distro jazzy to select Jazzy; Humble is the default.

run downloads the sample map, pulls the images, and starts the stack. The demo map is Copyright 2020 TIER IV, Inc. and is provided for demonstration only.

With --gpu, the planning service runs the planning-cuda image with planning_setting:=diffusion_planner, and run also downloads the Diffusion Planner v5.0 model from Hugging Face to ~/autoware_data/ml_models/diffusion_planner/v5.0. The first start builds a TensorRT engine from the model there, so it takes longer than later starts. Control and the rest of the stack are the same in both modes: control follows /planning/trajectory, whichever planner makes it. See Autoware Architecture 2.0 for the planner. Hosted CI runs the CPU mode; the GPU mode is checked on a GPU host.

Experimental

The GPU mode is experimental. Autoware 2.0.0's Diffusion Planner can stop the ego up to about 2 m before the goal, so the route does not become ARRIVED and run --gpu --verify fails on the sample route. This is the planner's own output, reproduced with upstream's image (autoware_universe#13603).

docs.title: Open the Visualizer
docs.text:
Open http://localhost:6080/vnc.html and sign in with the default password openadkit. Set your own REMOTE_PASSWORD in ~/.config/openadkit/<deployment>.env.

For a remote host, forward the port over SSH and open http://localhost:8080/vnc.html locally:

ssh -L 8080:localhost:6080 <user>@<host>

In RViz2, set an initial pose and a goal pose, then watch the vehicle drive the route. See the Autoware planning simulation guide for details.

openadkit stop

To replace missing or incomplete map data, run openadkit fetch planning-simulation --force. For other issues, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Scenario Simulation
docs.text:
Run predefined traffic scenarios with TIER IV Scenario Simulator. The deployment runs a scenario automatically and writes the results to the host. No GPU is required.

Complete the Quickstart setup first.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
Commands on this page are shown as installed by the release installer. From a source checkout, prefix them with ./ and run them from the repository root.

openadkit run scenario-simulation
openadkit logs --follow

Run Autoware on one host and the TIER IV runner on another with --node; see Split-host simulation.

Add --ros-distro jazzy to select Jazzy; Humble is the default.

run downloads the Kashiwanoha map. Autoware takes about 90 seconds to initialize; the runner then executes the scenario and writes the results to ~/openadkit-output/scenario-simulation/results (run prints the path).

docs.title: Open the Visualizer
docs.text:
Open http://localhost:6080/vnc.html and sign in with the default password openadkit. Set your own REMOTE_PASSWORD in ~/.config/openadkit/<deployment>.env.

For a remote host, forward the port over SSH and open http://localhost:8080/vnc.html locally:

ssh -L 8080:localhost:6080 <user>@<host>

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
Put overrides in ~/.config/openadkit/scenario-simulation.env:

Variable Purpose Default SCENARIO Scenario path inside the container Bundled example SCENARIO_HOST_DIR Host scenario directory, mounted at /scenarios ./scenarios OUTPUT_HOST_PATH Host results directory ~/openadkit-output/scenario-simulation/results SCENARIO_READY_TIMEOUT Seconds to wait for Autoware before running 600 GLOBAL_REAL_TIME_FACTOR Simulated seconds per wall-clock second; below 1 on a host that cannot run Autoware in real time 1.0 GLOBAL_TIMEOUT Wall-clock seconds each scenario may take; scale it with the factor 180 MAP_PATH Host map directory ~/autoware_map/kashiwanoha_map

A relative SCENARIO_HOST_DIR resolves from deployments/scenario-simulation/. MAP_PATH must be absolute; use $HOME rather than ~.

To run your own scenario, keep it outside the release. Create a directory, put the YAML there, and point the deployment at it in the host settings file:

SCENARIO_HOST_DIR=$HOME/openadkit-scenarios
SCENARIO=/scenarios/my-scenario.yaml

The default ./scenarios lies inside the installed release: files placed there mark the deployment as modified and are lost on upgrade or uninstall.

Scenarios must match the map, and the planning sample map does not work here. To use your own map, point MAP_PATH at a directory that holds the same files as the bundled map, which the CLI checks before starting: lanelet2_map.osm, pointcloud_map.pcd, global_map_center.pcd.yaml, lanelet2_map_provider.osm.yaml and map.map_publisher.yaml.

This deployment changes one Autoware parameter, in a file that holds only the changed value. On every start, the images merge it into the upstream parameter file: config/autoware/autoware_default_adapi_universe/config/default_adapi.param.yaml.

docs.text:

To replace missing map data, run openadkit fetch scenario-simulation --force. For other issues, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
For contributors and maintainers:

  • Build from Source: build the images locally, how CI builds them, and how releases are cut
  • Contributing: how to submit issues and pull requests
  • Evidence Workflow: reuse the verifier for a pinned build

docs.title: Build from Source
docs.text: How to build the Open AD Kit images locally, how CI builds them, and how releases are cut. Most users do not need this; pull the published images instead (see Container Images & Versioning).

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04 (openadkit setup supports Ubuntu only; elsewhere, install Docker with Buildx and Compose yourself)
  • Git, pipx, vcs2l, and python3-yaml to import the Autoware sources
  • Disk space for several multi-gigabyte images

The component Dockerfiles build on upstream Autoware images from GHCR and compile their package sets from a local autoware/src tree (step 4 below).

docs.title: Build System
docs.text:
Images are built with Docker Bake from components/docker-bake.hcl, the same file CI uses.

flowchart TB
    CORE["autoware:core-devel (build)<br/>autoware:base (runtime)"] --> UC["universe-common"]
    CUDA["autoware:base-cuda-{devel,runtime}"] --> SPC["sensing-perception-cuda"]

    UC --> SP["sensing-perception"]
    UC --> LM["localization-mapping"]
    UC --> PLN["planning"]
    UC --> CTL["control"]
    UC --> VS["vehicle-system"]
    UC --> API["api"]
    UC --> VIZ["visualizer"]
    UC --> SIM["simulator"]
    UC -.-> SPC

universe-common compiles the shared part of Autoware Universe on the upstream core-devel image and copies the result onto the lean upstream base image, so build tools never reach the runtime layers. Every component builds from it. sensing-perception-cuda builds on the upstream CUDA images and adds the universe-common install tree.

The published images end with a per-build Ubuntu security refresh. Components compile on universe-common-build, the devel image without that refresh, which CI pushes only to its build cache. Its digest changes only with its inputs, so a build that changes no Autoware source or component Dockerfile reuses the cached compiles and only refreshes and reassembles the runtime images.

Group Targets Published to universe-common universe-common-devel, universe-common ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/openadkit-common component all component images, including the amd64-only sensing-perception-cuda ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/openadkit planning-simulation universe-common plus the images Planning Simulation needs — (local builds) default universe-common + component —

docs.title: Build and Run Locally
docs.text:
# 1. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/autowarefoundation/openadkit.git
cd openadkit

# 2. Install host dependencies
./openadkit setup --verify

Activate the Docker group membership added by openadkit setup before running Docker without sudo. Either log out and back in, or run:

newgrp docker

# 3. Make the pipx-installed vcs command available in this shell
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

# 4. Import the Autoware sources this branch pins
AUTOWARE_REF=$(cat .github/autoware.ref)
git init autoware
git -C autoware fetch --depth 1 \
  https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware.git "$AUTOWARE_REF"
git -C autoware checkout --detach FETCH_HEAD
# An Autoware release, built on its official images
python3 .github/scripts/export_autoware_lock.py \
  autoware/repositories/autoware.repos autoware.lock
export UPSTREAM_TAG="$AUTOWARE_REF"
mkdir -p autoware/src
vcs import --shallow autoware/src < autoware.lock
mkdir -p autoware/src/middleware/external
touch autoware/src/middleware/external/.keep

# 5. Build the shared universe-common layer (~2 hours)
docker buildx bake -f components/docker-bake.hcl universe-common

# 6. Build the Planning Simulation images (~2 hours)
docker buildx bake -f components/docker-bake.hcl --load planning-simulation

# 7. Run with the local images
./openadkit run planning-simulation
  • --load puts the images in the local Docker store; without it, Bake only fills the build cache.
  • Local builds are tagged <target>-<arch>-<ros-distro> (for example planning-amd64-humble), which is the tag ./openadkit looks up in a source checkout. The arch follows the build host; when cross-building, set tags with --set <target>.tags=.... To use other images, set the *_IMAGE variables in ~/.config/openadkit/<deployment>.env.
  • For Jazzy, build with ROS_DISTRO=jazzy and run with --ros-distro jazzy.

Other useful targets:

docker buildx bake -f components/docker-bake.hcl                                # everything
docker buildx bake -f components/docker-bake.hcl component                      # all components
docker buildx bake -f components/docker-bake.hcl --load sensing-perception      # one image

docs.title: Build Variables
docs.text: Variable Description Default ROS_DISTRO humble or jazzy humble UPSTREAM_TAG Upstream Autoware release to build on, the tag in .github/autoware.ref (e.g. 2.0.0); required "" UPSTREAM_REPO Upstream Autoware image repository ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/autoware ROS_SNAPSHOT_HUMBLE, ROS_SNAPSHOT_JAZZY ROS apt snapshot the UPSTREAM_TAG images were built from. The build fails when they do not match; see ROS snapshot. Snapshots for 2.0.0

docs.title: Continuous Integration
docs.text:
build-all-images.yaml builds every target with the same Bake file. The build matrix comes from .github/image-inventory.json, the source of truth for which images are built and for which architectures.

Jobs run in dependency order: prepare, then build-common, then build-components. Most images build for Humble and Jazzy on amd64 and arm64. create-manifests then combines the per-arch images into multi-arch tags. CI disables the local tags (LOCAL_IMAGE="") and tags images through docker/metadata-action.

.github/autoware.ref pins the Autoware release a branch builds on its official images. CI builds main and release/* pushes, keeps registry caches per branch, and scans and runs the evidence cells after each build. A weekly scan of main's latest build opens a GitHub issue when it fails.

docs.title: Release Process
docs.text: Releases promote an existing CI build; nothing is rebuilt.

docs.title: Before You Release
docs.text:
• The branch: main, or a release/X.Y branch created from a release tag to fix an older line. Its .github/autoware.ref names the Autoware release (for example 2.0.0), and the ROS snapshots in components/docker-bake.hcl belong to that release.
  • vars.RUNNER_AMD64 and vars.RUNNER_ARM64 optionally move the build, scan and evidence jobs to larger runners (for example ubicloud-standard-8-ubuntu-2204 and ubicloud-standard-8-arm-ubuntu-2204). Unset, they run on the GitHub-hosted ubuntu-22.04 and ubuntu-22.04-arm. Pull request jobs run on them too, so point them only at ephemeral hosted runners, never at a persistent self-hosted machine.
  • GHCR packages accept pushes from CI: openadkit, openadkit-common, and openadkit-buildcache under ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/.
  • secrets.RELEASE_TOKEN (Contents and Workflows write) is set when promoting a build commit older than later workflow changes; otherwise GITHUB_TOKEN is used.
  • A successful build of build-all-images exists on that branch; stable and pre-releases vX.Y.Z both come from it. The build summary shows its build_tag. The release ships the CLI and deployments from that build's commit, and pushes that change only those start no build: dispatch build-all-images on the branch to release them. The release run warns when the branch has such changes.
  • A passing scan of scan-images exists for that build_tag on the same branch; it runs after the build.
  • A successful evidence run on the same branch passed every cell for that same build; it runs after the build. See Evidence Policy.
  • Highlights for a minor or major release are in .github/release-highlights/vX.Y.Z.md. The notes of that release and of its candidates open with them; the rest of the notes is generated.
  • The roadmap is reviewed for a minor or major release: finished items are gone, the release's items are under Now, and its Last reviewed line names the release. Validation checks that line for the release and its candidates.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
Run release.yaml on the build's branch with the version and build_tag. A release/X.Y branch releases with its own workflows and scripts, so a later main cannot change how an older line is validated. Its jobs run in order:

flowchart LR
    V[validate] --> P[package-bundles] --> R[publish] --> O[deploy-docs]
  1. validate: runs the release gates in validate_release.sh (version format, build provenance and age, scan results, metadata and file integrity, image coverage, passing L0-L2 evidence, registry digests, Git tag). Nothing is tagged if a gate fails.
  2. package-bundles: writes the immutable release plan and the runtime bundle for both distros.
  3. publish: writes notes/metadata from the validated plan, attests bundle/installer/plan/metadata and creates the draft with its assets. It then creates the image release tags and, for stable releases, the latest aliases (see Tag Reference), and publishes the draft, which creates the Git tag. A published release cannot be changed: a bad one is followed by the next version.
  4. deploy-docs: republishes the docs when the latest aliases moved.

The release plan (release-plan.json) attached to each GitHub Release records the exact image digests, aliases, assets, and checksums of that release.
