docs.title: Run the Evidence Workflow
docs.text: The reusable .github/workflows/evidence.yaml verifies a specific Open AD Kit build and publishes the run's summary. It runs automatically after a successful build-all-images run on main or a release/X.Y branch, which is the run a release of that build needs.

docs.title: Reuse it in the build-owning repository
docs.text:
A caller workflow in the same repository (or a fork hosting the same build and evidence workflows) can call it without duplicating the runner:

name: verify-existing-build
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      build_tag:
        description: Build run ID and attempt, e.g. 123456789-1
        required: true
        type: string

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: read

jobs:
  evidence:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/evidence.yaml
    with:
      build_tag: ${{ inputs.build_tag }}

This runs containers on the caller's runners. A fork's evidence runs belong to that fork; only runs on the branch that built the release, in the releasing repository, can be release evidence.

The current reusable interface takes only build_tag. Metadata and source come from the caller's build-owning repository. It stages that exact source's reference deployments and the example kit, which the staged CLI's openadkit new makes with the fixture in .github/scripts/evidence/kit on top. It does not take an arbitrary external kit repository, revision or scenario as input. Do not copy this example into an unrelated integrator repository and claim it verifies that kit; external kit intake needs a dedicated, pinned, trusted-builder implementation before such a claim is valid.

docs.title: Inputs, outputs and boundaries
docs.text:
build_tag has the form <run_id>-<run_attempt>. The matching build-metadata-<build_tag> artifact must be available in the repository. The workflow checks out its openadkit_sha and stages runtime image digests from the same metadata, never latest aliases. It stages and verifies the kit with the same step that assembles release bundles, so the cells run the tree a release of that build ships, plus the example kit.

The example workspace builds against that build's matching distro-specific universe-common-devel digest. Source/config checksums omit build, install and log products. Hosted runners execute L0-L2 cells, retry a failed cell once, and aggregate all expected cells, including missing-cell failures.

The workflow uploads per-cell diagnostics and the evidence-summary-<build_tag> artifact. The release gate reads that summary; see the release policy.

Runner cells use schemaVersion: 1, and the summary (schemaVersion: 3) carries them as written. Readers accept only these versioned payloads: a cell without schemaVersion: 1 and metrics is rejected. Summary readers should use metrics rather than top-level timings.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
From zero to a running Autoware planning simulation in about 10 minutes. No GPU is required.

  1. 1 Get the kitDownload or clone
  2. 2 Set up the hostConfigure dependencies
  3. 3 Run simulationStart planning
  4. 4 Open visualizerInspect the output
  5. 5 DriveSet a route

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ubuntu 22.04 (Jammy) or 24.04 (Noble) with sudo access
  • curl for the release installer; python3 and tar are preinstalled on supported Ubuntu releases
  • A web browser - the visualizer runs in it, no display server needed

docs.title: 1. Get Open AD Kit
docs.text:
Release bundles

Each stable GitHub Release will publish a versionless openadkit installer and one openadkit-vX.Y.Z.tar.gz containing the runtime entry point and the curated deployments (planning, logging, scenario, CARLA, and Safety Island). Split-host nodes ship as experimental. Images and sample data are pulled on demand. Until the first release exists, use a source checkout.

Source checkoutRelease bundle 
git clone https://github.com/autowarefoundation/openadkit.git
cd openadkit

Download the latest release. The command verifies the release bundle before installing it to ~/.local/share/openadkit and makes openadkit available from ~/.local/bin.

curl -fsSL https://github.com/autowarefoundation/openadkit/releases/latest/download/openadkit \
  | bash -s -- install

If ~/.local/bin is not on your PATH, the installer prints the command to add it. For a reproducible install, replace latest with a release version and pass the same version to install:

curl -fsSL https://github.com/autowarefoundation/openadkit/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/openadkit \
  | bash -s -- install --version vX.Y.Z

To verify the bundle yourself before running it, see Verify a Release Bundle Manually.

The release bundle contains only the runtime and deployment assets. A source checkout also contains the image sources, CI, and development tools.

docs.title: 2. Set Up the Host
docs.text:
After a release install, these commands work from any directory. For a source checkout, prefix them with ./ (for example ./openadkit) and run them from the repository root.

openadkit setup --verify

Run setup as your normal user. It requests sudo only for host changes. CPU is the default; add --gpu for NVIDIA deployments. --gpu also installs NVIDIA OpenGL/Vulkan libraries needed for CARLA. Setup installs Docker only when the host has none; it never replaces an existing engine. If Docker is installed but Docker Compose 5.0 or newer is missing, install Docker's docker-compose-plugin (instructions) and rerun setup. Ubuntu's own docker-compose-v2 package is too old.

Activate the Docker group membership added by openadkit setup before running Docker without sudo. Either log out and back in, or run:

newgrp docker

docs.title: 3. Run Planning Simulation
docs.text:
openadkit run planning-simulation

Add --ros-distro jazzy to select Jazzy. Humble is the default in both source checkouts and release bundles.

run downloads and verifies the sample map, pulls missing images, starts the services, and waits until they are ready.

docs.title: 4. Open the Visualizer
docs.text:
Once run returns, Autoware is ready. Open:

http://localhost:6080/vnc.html

Use the default password openadkit.

To open RViz on your own desktop instead of the browser, set REMOTE_DISPLAY=false in ~/.config/openadkit/<deployment>.env; the visualizer then uses your session's DISPLAY and XAUTHORITY.

For a remote host, keep noVNC loopback-only and forward it over SSH:

ssh -L 8080:localhost:6080 <user>@<host>

Then open http://localhost:8080/vnc.html locally.

docs.title: 5. Drive
docs.text:
In RViz2, follow the Autoware planning simulation instructions to:

  1. Set an initial pose for the ego vehicle
  2. Set a goal pose on the map
  3. Watch the vehicle plan and drive the route

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
Explore the other deployments - scenario testing, rosbag replay, and CARLA. Split-host (--node over Zenoh) is experimental.

  • CLI & Maintenance - Runtime controls, validation, upgrades, and cleanup
  • Components - The architecture behind what you just ran
  • Container Images & Versioning - Tag schema and pinning guidance
  • Create a Kit - Build your own stack on a deployment

docs.title: CLI & Maintenance
docs.text:
Commands you need after the first run: runtime controls, validation, configuration, upgrades, and cleanup.

Commands on this page are shown as installed by the release installer. From a source checkout, prefix them with ./ and run them from the repository root.

docs.title: Short Name and Tab Completion
docs.text: openadkit install also links adkit, a short name for the same launcher: adkit run planning-simulation is openadkit run planning-simulation. Tab completes commands, options and deployment names, for both names: those of the kit around the current directory, or else of the active release; bash-completion (installed on Ubuntu by default) loads it from ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions in a new shell. The installer leaves an adkit or a completion file that it did not install alone, and openadkit uninstall removes only its own links.

docs.title: Runtime Controls
docs.text:
openadkit status
openadkit logs --follow
openadkit logs map planning        # only these services
openadkit restart                  # services reread config and overlay workspaces
openadkit restart --all            # the whole deployment, with the same settings
openadkit shell                    # a shell in the api service with ROS sourced
openadkit shell planning ros2 node list
openadkit record /tf /localization/kinematic_state
openadkit stop

These act on the deployment running on this host, from any directory, so they take no deployment name. When several nodes of a split deployment run on one host, pick one with --node; status and stop act on all of them.

restart with no service restarts every service that takes Open AD Kit config or an overlay workspace, so a changed parameter file or a rebuilt workspace applies without restarting a simulator such as CARLA; it names the services it left running. restart --all restarts the whole deployment in place, one-shot services included, as a fresh start with the same settings. Like run, it returns once the restarted services are ready, fails if one crashes, and warns about overrides that changed nothing. Changes to Compose files or .env values need stop and run again. shell sources ROS, Autoware and the overlay workspaces like the services' entrypoint; give it a service and a command to run one command instead.

Below its services, status shows Autoware's state from the AD API:

localization initialized
routing      set
mode         stop (autonomous available)
mrm          normal

A line reads no data while nothing publishes that state yet, for example before localization starts.

record writes a rosbag of the named topics (or --all) to ~/openadkit-output/<deployment>/recordings/ (--output to change) until Ctrl+C. It runs as a copy of the running api container, so it joins the deployment's ROS domain and knows the overlay's message types, and the bag stays on the host when the deployment stops. One deployment runs at a time, including deployments from other kits, even one with the same name. run refuses conflicting projects; stop them first with openadkit stop. Declared split nodes of the same deployment can still run together. run returns once the deployment is ready: its services' healthchecks pass, for example once the AD API is up (READINESS_CHECKS in the deployment's config.env). It then watches the services for 10 seconds and fails if one crashes. openadkit run <deployment> --verify then runs the deployment's verify step, the check CI runs on it: Planning Simulation drives the ego from its start to its goal, Scenario Simulation waits for the scenarios' result. run --verify exits with the step's result; the deployment keeps running. Every run writes results/run.json in the deployment's output directory: the version, distro and images it started, the digest of the resolved Compose model, content digests of the config layers and overlay workspace it mounts, how long it took to be ready and, with --verify, the step's result. openadkit run <deployment> --pull always refreshes images before starting, and openadkit version prints the installed version. --no-visualizer starts everything except the visualizer, for a host nobody watches; its software-rendered RViz needs CPU that Autoware lacks on a small host. CI evidence runs this way.

docs.title: Validate Before Running
docs.text:
openadkit validate planning-simulation --data

validate checks the manifest and the Compose configuration without starting anything. --data also reports each data resource as ok, missing, incomplete, or outdated and fails on any gap. It follows the same GPU selection as run: use openadkit validate logging-simulation --gpu --data to include the CenterPoint models.

Commands print what they do in plain terms; add --verbose (or set OPENADKIT_VERBOSE=1) to also see the docker commands they run, status queries aside.

list, version, and validate accept --json for scripting; validate --json prints one JSON document also when the deployment is invalid ("valid": false with the "error"). config prints the resolved Compose model of a deployment as JSON; it takes validate's --ros-distro, --gpu, --node and --ws; AutoSD builds on it.

validate, config, fetch, run and clean also take a deployment's directory instead of its name, such as openadkit run ./my-kit: an argument with a / or a leading . is a directory, and the kit around it is used wherever you run the command.

docs.title: Your Own Kit
docs.text: openadkit new my-kit [--base DEPLOYMENT] makes ./my-kit, a kit on top of a deployment of this Open AD Kit (Planning Simulation by default) that holds only your differences. See Create a Kit.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Each deployment reads its settings from environment files, in this order (later files win):

  1. deployments/<name>/config.env: the deployment defaults
  2. deployments/<name>/config.gpu.env: GPU settings, loaded only with --gpu
  3. ~/.config/openadkit/<name>.env: your host settings

Shell exports do not override variables defined in these files. Put host settings such as MAP_PATH or REMOTE_PASSWORD in your host settings file. It lives outside the release, so upgrades keep it. Source checkouts can also override component images there; release images stay pinned.

Directory Default Override Host settings ~/.config/openadkit OPENADKIT_CONFIG_DIR (or XDG_CONFIG_HOME) Results and recordings ~/openadkit-output/<name>/{results,recordings} OPENADKIT_OUTPUT_DIR

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
openadkit upgrade --check   # report whether a newer stable version exists
openadkit upgrade           # install it

The new release is verified and installed next to the old one, and the openadkit launcher is repointed. The previous version stays in the install destination (default ~/.local/share/openadkit/), so you can roll back:

openadkit install --version vOLD --force

--force replaces the kept version directory; omit it to install a version that is not kept. Source checkouts update with git pull instead.

docs.title: Uninstall and Cleanup
docs.text:
Stop running deployments first; uninstall refuses while any is running, because it removes the launcher that openadkit stop needs.

openadkit stop
openadkit uninstall          # keep previously installed versions
openadkit uninstall --all    # remove kept versions too

uninstall is for release installs; remove a source checkout with Git. Host settings in ~/.config/openadkit and results and recordings in ~/openadkit-output are kept.

Downloaded data (maps, rosbags, and perception models) lives under ~/autoware_map and ~/autoware_data and is kept by uninstall. Check and delete a deployment's data with:

openadkit validate planning-simulation --data   # report
openadkit clean planning-simulation             # delete, after asking

clean lists what it deletes and asks first; --yes skips the question, as scripts need. It deletes all the data the deployment uses, so a kit or a deployment on a base also deletes the base's data (the list says so); the next run or fetch downloads it again.

clean and fetch --force refuse while that deployment is running, or when any live container mounts the data (including another kit or deployment). If data usage cannot be checked, deletion or replacement is refused. If Scenario Simulation's Kashiwanoha map is removed, restore it with openadkit fetch scenario-simulation --force.

run downloads missing data, but never replaces an existing data directory. Replace incomplete or outdated managed data explicitly with fetch --force; run --force is not supported. Managed data is outdated when the deployment now declares other content for it, for example a fixed map with a new checksum: run, fetch and validate --data then stop and ask for fetch --force.

The CLI marks the data it installs with a .openadkit-resource.json file. clean and --force only delete or replace marked data. Data that was already there, such as a map you copied yourself, is still used when it is complete, but the CLI never deletes or replaces it; move or remove it yourself.

docs.title: Split-host nodes
docs.text:
validate and run accept --node for split-host simulation. status, logs, and stop find the live node from its Compose project; pass --node only when several nodes of one deployment run on the same machine.

Each node's declared Compose entrypoint owns its full service graph, including any bridge. The CLI selects those files and the node's ROS domain; it never adds a networking service behind the scenes. With --verbose, the printed Compose command shows the selected files, env files and project name (openadkit-<deployment>_<node>).

docs.title: Verify a Release Bundle Manually
docs.text:
To inspect a release before running anything, download the bundle and check it against the release metadata:

VERSION=$(curl -fsSL \
  https://api.github.com/repos/autowarefoundation/openadkit/releases/latest \
  | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["tag_name"])')
curl -fLO "https://github.com/autowarefoundation/openadkit/releases/download/${VERSION}/openadkit-${VERSION}.tar.gz"
curl -fLO "https://github.com/autowarefoundation/openadkit/releases/download/${VERSION}/release-metadata.json"
EXPECTED=$(python3 -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("release-metadata.json"))["bundles"][0]["sha256"])')
printf '%s  %s\n' "$EXPECTED" "openadkit-${VERSION}.tar.gz" | sha256sum --check -
tar -xzf "openadkit-${VERSION}.tar.gz"
cd "openadkit-${VERSION}"

The extracted directory is a complete runtime; run it with ./openadkit.

docs.title: Container Images & Versioning
docs.text: Open AD Kit publishes images to the GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/openadkit). This page is the reference for image tags, versions, and what "supported" means.

docs.title: Tag Reference
docs.text:
Releases are promoted from existing CI builds rather than rebuilt, so the images tested in CI are the images that ship. Every tag below points at a promoted image digest.

Tag Example Created Moves? Release planning-humble-v2.0.0 Every release No Latest alias planning-humble Stable releases Yes Pre-release planning-humble-v2.0.0-rc.1 Pre-releases No CI build planning-humble-123456789-1 Every CI build (<run_id>-<run_attempt>) No

Releases promote a CI build of main (see Versioning).

Pre-releases never move the latest aliases. No alias leaves out the distro, so an image never switches ROS distro under the same tag.

Examples use Humble, the default distro. Jazzy images use the same patterns with -jazzy (for example planning-jazzy). sensing-perception-cuda and planning-cuda are amd64-only, and only the amd64 simulator carries the CARLA client.

docs.title: Choosing a Tag
docs.text:
• Reproducible deployments: use a release tag (vX.Y.Z) or a digest.
  • Latest stable for a distro: use <target>-<ros_distro>.
  • Never pin per-platform CI tags such as universe-common-amd64-humble; they move with every build of main.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
Open AD Kit versions follow Semantic Versioning on their own, starting at v2.0.0: a backward-incompatible change to the CLI, the manifests or a deployment raises the major version, and a move to a new Autoware release raises at least the minor version. The release notes list what breaks.

Releases come from main, which pins one Autoware release in .github/autoware.ref. Every release pairs the two in its GitHub Release title, Open AD Kit v2.0.1 · Autoware 2.0.0, and so do openadkit install and openadkit version. The release also pins the ROS 2 distros and every image digest, and its images carry org.opencontainers.image.autoware-base-version. A fix that is upstream but not yet in an Autoware release can be backported; the release notes list it, and the Autoware version stays the tag's. A release/X.Y branch is created from a release tag only to fix an older version.

docs.title: ROS 2 Distro Support
docs.text:
Distro Status Humble Default Jazzy Published where required builds, scans and runtime evidence pass

A release bundle carries pinned images for both distros; choose one with --ros-distro. A distro is supported only while it is supported upstream. Non-exempt evidence cells for each declared distro must also pass the release evidence gate. The initial default is Humble; changing it requires a reviewed manifest change and passing evidence, not an automatic release-time fallback. Image builds alone do not prove runtime behavior on every architecture.

docs.title: ROS Package Snapshot
docs.text:
Every image installs its ROS packages from one dated ROS snapshot: the one the upstream Autoware images of that release were built from. Compiled code and runtime therefore use the same ROS versions, and the build fails if they would differ. The release BOM names the snapshot per distro; an image carries it as a label:

docker inspect --format '{{ index .Config.Labels "org.opencontainers.image.ros-snapshot" }}' \
  ghcr.io/autowarefoundation/openadkit:planning-humble

The snapshot changes only with the upstream Autoware release. Ubuntu packages are not pinned, so security updates keep flowing into new builds.

docs.title: What "Supported" Means
docs.text:
• Releases: the latest stable release is supported. Fixes, including CVE remediation, ship in a new release; older releases are not patched.
  • Platforms: support is tiered (committed, experimental, best-effort, unsupported). See Supported Platforms.
  • No certification claims: Open AD Kit makes no safety-certification, functional-safety, or production-readiness claims.

Community help and version coverage are described in SUPPORT.md; report security vulnerabilities through the private reporting policy.

Maintainers: see the Release Process.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Commands on this page are shown as installed by the release installer. From a source checkout, prefix them with ./ and run them from the repository root.

docs.title: Permission denied
docs.text: Your user must be in the docker group. Log out and back in after openadkit setup, or run newgrp docker. Do not run openadkit with sudo.

docs.title: A deployment fails to start
docs.text:
1. Check that Docker is running: docker info.
  2. Check the configuration: openadkit validate <deployment> --data.
  3. Read the logs: openadkit logs --follow.

If run fails after the containers are created, they keep running so you can read their logs. Stop them with openadkit stop.

docs.title: Missing or incomplete maps, rosbags, or models
docs.text:
openadkit validate <deployment> --data
openadkit fetch <deployment> --force

validate --data reports each resource as ok, missing, or incomplete; add --gpu to it for Logging Simulation's CenterPoint models (CARLA always runs in GPU mode). fetch always includes GPU data. --force only replaces data the CLI installed; remove data you placed yourself, then run openadkit fetch <deployment>.

docs.title: NVIDIA Container Toolkit not detected
docs.text:
• Install it with openadkit setup --gpu --verify.
  • Check the GPU: nvidia-smi and nvidia-ctk --version.
  • Restart Docker: sudo systemctl restart docker.

docs.title: Perception is slow
docs.text: The default perception image runs on CPU. For CUDA perception, run Logging Simulation with --gpu on an amd64 host with an NVIDIA GPU. The CUDA image does not fall back to CPU.

docs.title: Blank visualizer
docs.text: Wait 10 to 30 seconds after run, then reload the page. If it stays blank, check openadkit logs --follow.

docs.title: noVNC says "failed to connect"
docs.text: Open the page over http://. Releases up to v2.0.0-rc.7 served noVNC over HTTPS with a certificate generated at each start: the browser loaded the page from its cache, never asked about the new certificate, and the WebSocket to it failed (the visualizer log shows SSLV3_ALERT_CERTIFICATE_UNKNOWN). The visualizer now serves plain HTTP unless you give it a certificate (NOVNC_CERT, NOVNC_KEY).

docs.title: Port 6080 already in use
docs.text: Port 6080 serves the visualizer. Stop the service that holds the port. The CLI deployments use host networking, so adding a ports: mapping to docker-compose.yaml has no effect.

docs.title: Point clouds arrive at a lower rate than they are published
docs.text:
Large messages need large UDP buffers between the containers. deployments/shared/cyclonedds.xml requests them, and openadkit setup raises the kernel limits that cap them (/etc/sysctl.d/99-openadkit-dds.conf). Check the limit and whether the kernel drops packets:

sysctl net.core.rmem_max      # 2147483647 after setup
nstat -az UdpRcvbufErrors     # a growing count means drops

docs.title: ROS 2 nodes on another machine cannot see the stack
docs.text:
DDS stays on loopback by default. To reach other hosts, set CYCLONEDDS_NETWORK_INTERFACE to the exact LAN or VPN interface name in your host settings file (~/.config/openadkit/<deployment>.env):

CYCLONEDDS_NETWORK_INTERFACE=eth0

This applies to single-host runs; a split-host node always keeps DDS on loopback and reaches the other host through its Zenoh bridge. ROS_DOMAIN_ID separates traffic but provides no authentication or encryption.

docs.text:

  • Autoware Foundation Discord

docs.title: Supported Platforms
docs.text:
Deployments run on Ubuntu with Docker Compose for development and simulation. Platforms are edge targets on automotive operating systems such as AutoSD.

Open AD Kit is the first SOAFEE blueprint, co-developed with SOAFEE and the eSync Alliance; DENSO's AVP blueprint and Red Hat's AutoSD blueprint build on it.

AutoSD

The upstream preview of Red Hat In-Vehicle OS. Containers run under Podman and systemd with mixed-criticality partitions.

AutoSD

EWAOL

Arm's container-centric Yocto framework and the original SOAFEE reference. Background only; not an Open AD Kit target.

EWAOL

docs.title: Support Matrix
docs.text:
A path that fails its build or validation gate is dropped or marked here, not documented as if it worked. Individual boards are listed on the Hardware page.

Path Tier Notes Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 + Docker Compose deployments Committed Compose validated in CI; CARLA runs on 22.04 only Component images, amd64 + arm64 Committed sensing-perception-cuda is amd64-only; only the amd64 simulator carries the CARLA client Jazzy images Best-effort Published where the builds pass; Humble is the default CARLA deployment Experimental Humble, amd64, NVIDIA GPU AutoSD with Podman and Quadlet Experimental Component images, generated from Compose; Planning Simulation only EWAOL Unsupported No assets in this repository

Other Linux distributions may work but are not tested.

docs.title: AutoSD
docs.text:
AutoSD (Automotive Stream Distribution) is the public, in-development preview of Red Hat In-Vehicle OS. It is built on CentOS Stream with an automotive kernel and provides:

  • Mixed criticality: safety-critical containers in the root partition, non-critical ones in an isolated QM partition
  • Atomic updates: immutable OSTree images with A/B updates and rollback
  • Real-time kernel for deterministic scheduling
  • Container-native runtime: Podman, Quadlet (systemd container units), and BlueChi orchestration, with no Docker daemon

docs.title: Generate a Deployment
docs.text:
Compose stays the single source. openadkit config prints a deployment's resolved Compose model, and platforms/autosd/quadlet.py translates it:

openadkit fetch planning-simulation
openadkit config planning-simulation \
  | python3 platforms/autosd/quadlet.py --output out --without visualizer \
      --root-password-hash "$(openssl passwd -6 password)"

Use the openadkit of an installed release and platforms/autosd from the same tag: the release's CLI puts the image digests in the model, so the result is pinned. From a source checkout the images are latest aliases. Kits work the same way, such as openadkit config ./my-kit.

Output Contents out/rootfs/etc/containers/systemd/ A Quadlet unit per service, named after its container out/rootfs/usr/share/openadkit/ The bind-mounted files and data, by mount target out/image.aib.yml Automotive Image Builder manifest that embeds the images and rootfs/; written only with --root-password-hash, since an image has no default password

A Compose field the script does not translate stops it instead of being dropped. It covers what Planning Simulation uses; writable mounts, for example, have no translation yet.

The units run as root with the deployment's host networking. They use the component images, and mapping them onto AutoSD's root and QM partitions is not done yet.

Evidence scope

Evidence runs these units under Podman and systemd on Ubuntu 24.04 and drives the ego to its goal. CI does not build or boot the image below. An image built from these units was driven once by hand: it booted in QEMU with SELinux enforcing and no outside network, and the ego arrived at its goal.

docs.title: Run on a Podman Host
docs.text:
The tree is what an image would contain, so a host with Podman 4.9 or newer, catatonit and systemd can run it:

sudo cp -a out/rootfs/. /
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl start autoware-api autoware-control autoware-perception-simulation \
  autoware-planning autoware-simulator autoware-system autoware-vehicle
systemctl status 'autoware-*'
journalctl -u autoware-control -f

Quadlet registers each .container file as a .service unit. The units pull their images on first start, which takes a while.

docs.title: Build an Image
docs.text:
You need Podman and QEMU; the runner does not work with Docker. Download the Automotive Image Builder runner and build its container:

curl -fL -o auto-image-builder.sh \
  "https://gitlab.com/CentOS/automotive/src/automotive-image-builder/-/raw/main/auto-image-builder.sh?ref_type=heads"
chmod +x auto-image-builder.sh
sudo bash ./auto-image-builder.sh build-builder --distro autosd10-sig

Build the image from the directory you generated out in, because the manifest names its large files by path. /var/tmp goes on disk because the runner's own is in memory and too small for this image. The arguments are the manifest, the container image name, and the disk image to write:

sudo mkdir -p /var/tmp/aib-work
sudo AIB_PODMAN_OPTIONS="-v /var/tmp/aib-work:/var/tmp" bash ./auto-image-builder.sh build \
  --distro autosd10-sig \
  --target qemu \
  --define-file platforms/autosd/vars.yml \
  out/image.aib.yml \
  localhost/openadkit:latest \
  disk.qcow2
sudo chown "$(logname)" disk.qcow2

To run Automotive Image Builder directly instead, use an RPM-based host (Fedora, CentOS, or RHEL) with Automotive Image Builder, OSBuild, and QEMU installed.

docs.title: Run the Image
docs.text:
With air installed:

air disk.qcow2

Or with QEMU directly:

/usr/bin/qemu-system-x86_64 \
  -drive file=/usr/share/OVMF/OVMF_CODE.fd,if=pflash,format=raw,unit=0,readonly=on \
  -drive file=/usr/share/OVMF/OVMF_VARS.fd,if=pflash,format=raw,unit=1,snapshot=on,readonly=off \
  -smp 20 \
  -nographic \
  -enable-kvm \
  -m 16384 \
  -machine q35 \
  -cpu host \
  -device virtio-net-pci,netdev=n0,mac=FE:00:e2:0d:ba:4d \
  -netdev user,id=n0,net=10.0.2.0/24,hostfwd=tcp::2222-:22 \
  -drive file=disk.qcow2,index=0,media=disk,format=qcow2,if=virtio,id=rootdisk,snapshot=off

-m 16384 (16 GB) is the minimum for the Autoware stack; use -m 32768 for heavier workloads. -m 2G is enough only to boot and explore the OS. Log in as root with the password password from the command above, which is for this demo only.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text:
No stable release has been published yet. Until the first release, run Open AD Kit from a source checkout.

GitHub Releases is the canonical source for published versions, release notes, and provenance metadata. Each stable release publishes:

  • a versionless openadkit installer
  • the versioned openadkit-vX.Y.Z.tar.gz bundle
  • the pinned Autoware meta-release, ROS 2 distro(s), and image tags and digests
  • a BOM, the passing runtime evidence summary, explicit CI exemptions and default distro
  • build provenance for the installer, bundle, plan and metadata

The notes open with the release's highlights and install command, list the merged pull requests by type, and summarize the runtime evidence. Installed releases move to the latest stable version with openadkit upgrade. Tag naming is documented in Container Images & Versioning. See Evidence Policy for the blocking gate and verification report, and Verify a Release before executing downloaded artifacts.

Planned work and its priority order are on the Roadmap.

docs.title: Evidence and Release Policy
docs.text: A release promotes an existing build. It does not rebuild images or silently relax its tests. Both stable releases and release candidates require a successful evidence run that passed every cell for the promoted build.

docs.title: What the gate checks
docs.text:
Before creating a tag, the release validation job looks for an evidence-summary-<build_tag> artifact and accepts it only when:

  1. The run succeeded: it is a completed, successful run of .github/workflows/evidence.yaml on the branch that built the release.
  2. It tested this build: the summary names the promoted build tag, and it tested the build's own commit, not another commit against its images.
  3. Every cell passed: the summary result is PASSED. A cell passes only when L0, L1 and L2 all pass, and a missing expected cell fails the run.

A passing rerun may supersede a failed run; a failed run never counts. There is no release bypass input. The release also requires the latest full scan of the build to pass.

docs.title: Cells and levels
docs.text:
Evidence cells are enumerated from the source deployment manifests:

Deployment Distros Topologies Planning Simulation Humble, Jazzy Single host; also under Podman and systemd with the AutoSD units Scenario Simulation Humble, Jazzy Single host; two isolated nodes on one host example-kit: a kit made with openadkit new, plus a fixture that uses every extension point Humble, Jazzy Planning Simulation extended with the fixture's C++ overlay Safety Island Simulation Humble, Jazzy Planning Simulation driven by the pinned Safety Island release over domain_bridge

The example kit gates a release like every other cell: it shows that each kit extension point works on the build. It does not verify integrators' own kits.

All currently run on GitHub-hosted linux/amd64 runners. Image build and scan coverage includes the inventory's other architectures; this must not be presented as arm64 runtime, two-machine LAN, GPU, HIL or vehicle evidence.

  • L0: manifests and Compose configuration validate.
  • L1: openadkit run returns: the deployment's healthchecks pass, so its ROS interfaces are present and its topics publish.
  • L2: the deployment's verify step passes (openadkit run --verify): the Planning Simulation ego arrives at its goal, or the scenarios pass, plus the split-node checks. Each run starts a fresh stack.

The workflow retries a failed evidence cell once. A cell that still fails fails the run and blocks a release. The cells start deployments with openadkit run --no-visualizer.

A 4-vCPU GitHub-hosted runner cannot run Autoware in real time: the ego drives late and the bundled samples take about three times as long as on a 16-vCPU host. The scenario-simulation cells therefore run the simulation at half speed (GLOBAL_REAL_TIME_FACTOR=0.5, with GLOBAL_TIMEOUT=400 wall-clock seconds) through the cell's host settings file, so they test the scenarios rather than the runner's size. Investigate a cell that still fails after the workflow's retry.

docs.title: Testing a change without a build
docs.text:
A change that rebuilds no image, such as a deployment setting, the CLI or a check, runs the cells against an existing build:

  • A pull request that touches deployments/, cli/ or the evidence checks runs them against its base branch's latest successful build. When it also changes an image's inputs, it waits for the build after merge instead.
  • A dispatch of evidence.yaml with source_ref tests that branch or commit; build_tag defaults to the dispatched branch's latest successful build.

The cells take the deployments, CLI and checks from the tested commit and the images from the build. Such a run is not release evidence: its summary names both commits, which the gate rejects.

docs.title: Explicit CI exemptions
docs.text:
CARLA Simulation requires a GPU; Logging Simulation has no hosted runtime cell. Their deployment manifests contain a reasoned evidence.exempt entry. They remain in the bundle, are listed in release metadata/notes, and the CLI warns when they run. An exemption is not runtime evidence.

Planning Simulation's cells run its CPU mode. Its GPU mode (--gpu, the Diffusion Planner on planning-cuda) has no hosted evidence cell; it is checked on a GPU host and validated (L0) in CI.

Adding an exemption is a reviewed source change, not a release-time override. Do not use it to hide a known product failure in a normally tested cell.

docs.title: Autoware and ROS distro decisions
docs.text:
Pin the latest stable Autoware release at the release cut. If it has a blocking issue, keep the previous verified stable pin and explain the exception, date and follow-up in the release notes.

Every release, stable or candidate, is a build of main (or of a release/X.Y branch that fixes an older line) on the Autoware release tag in .github/autoware.ref. The release records that Autoware version; the build's autoware-lock.repos, resolved SHA and upstream image digests record the input.

docs.title: Backporting an Autoware fix
docs.text:
Autoware releases come months apart. A fix that blocks a release and is upstream, merged on Autoware's main or in an open pull request, can ride on the pinned release as a patch instead of waiting for the next Autoware release:

  1. In the upstream repository, git format-patch -1 <commit>, and add a line Upstream: <URL of the commit or pull request> to its message.
  2. Open a pull request into main (or the release/X.Y branch) that adds it as .github/autoware-patches/<repository>/<NNNN>-<subject>.patch, where <repository> is its path under autoware/src (a key of autoware-lock.repos, such as universe/autoware_universe). The review is the fix's own diff.
  3. Every build applies the patches in order right after vcs import; one that does not apply, or has no Upstream: line, fails the build. The release lists them under Backported Autoware fixes, its bundle carries them as autoware.backports, and openadkit version counts them. The Autoware version stays that of the tag.
  4. When the branch moves to an Autoware release that contains the fix, delete the patch.

defaultRosDistro in the promoted openadkit.json explicitly selects the ROS distro, and its required evidence cells must pass. The gate does not automatically switch from Humble to Jazzy or remove a failing distro. To change supported distros, update the manifests in a reviewed source change and build/test that revision. Humble remains the initial default.

docs.title: Metadata and verification report
docs.text:
release-plan.json seals the selected evidence summary (result, build, commit, run URL and cells) before packaging. release-metadata.json includes that same evidence, the BOM and the CI exemptions. Bundle, installer, plan and metadata receive release-workflow build provenance.

The verification table shows passing-cell count, readiness time, arrival time and peak memory for the current build. Release never searches older runs or releases; its notes depend only on the release plan. Missing metrics are shown as -, never replaced with zeroes.

See Verify a Release and Run the Evidence Workflow.

docs.title: Verify a Release
docs.text: Verify downloaded files before executing the installer. Use a recent GitHub CLI with gh attestation and jq. Older previews may not have these attestations or metadata fields.

docs.title: Download and verify release artifacts
docs.text:
Replace the example version with the release you intend to use:

set -euo pipefail
VERSION=v2.0.0
BRANCH=main  # or the release/X.Y branch that released it
REPO=autowarefoundation/openadkit
gh release download "$VERSION" --repo "$REPO" \
  --pattern openadkit --pattern "openadkit-$VERSION.tar.gz" \
  --pattern release-plan.json --pattern release-metadata.json

for asset in openadkit "openadkit-$VERSION.tar.gz" release-plan.json release-metadata.json; do
  gh attestation verify "$asset" --repo "$REPO" \
    --signer-workflow "$REPO/.github/workflows/release.yaml" \
    --source-ref "refs/heads/$BRANCH" --deny-self-hosted-runners
done

The default predicate verifies SLSA build provenance. Provenance binds the bytes to the release workflow; it does not establish that runtime tests passed.

Cross-check the plan and bundle hashes recorded in the verified metadata:

printf '%s  %s\n' "$(jq -r '.release_plan_sha256' release-metadata.json)" release-plan.json \
  | sha256sum --check
jq -r '.bundles[] | .sha256 + "  " + .name' release-metadata.json \
  | sha256sum --check

Review .release, .releaseContext and .evidence in the plan: the requested version, promoted commit, default distro, passing cells and CI exemptions. The metadata's .evidence must match the plan's .evidence exactly, and its url links the evidence run the release gate accepted.

After verification, install the downloaded launcher or use the documented installation flow. Evidence is bounded to the tested cells; it is not a vehicle-safety or security certification.
